why: Rule 1 at a 92-degree deg-2 kink: the 7.7cm proton stub rises 128k to 230k away toward 20001 while the 162cm muon stays flat MIP and exits at z=499; 20002 is also the lowest-z end.

Abstain: no junction anywhere in the event survives rule 1; the sole multi-prong candidate 33026 opens at 138 degrees with its longer prong rising toward it, and all eight dQ/dx profiles are flat MIP with no Bragg at any end.

Only real object is a 43cm MIP track whose 15000 end sits on the x=-201 anode face, so 15001 is the contained end; it is lower in z and the segment rises away from it, with debris blobs spraying downstream.

Rule 1 perfectly satisfied at a deg-3 star: all three prongs rise away, with the 111cm muon showing a monotone rise to 145k on the stopping-muon template and both protons following the proton template to their stops.

The 53.8cm muon has a genuine monotone Bragg rising 45k to 125k over its last 15cm at 18001 and the 4.3cm proton stub rises 45k to 215k away to 18003, so both prongs stop away from this fully contained junction.

97-degree kink where the 40cm pion shows a real decaying Bragg at 14004 and the 113cm muon runs flat MIP out through the y=+198 top face; the hot reading at 14002 is one shared 330k junction point, the hot-blob trap, not a Bragg.

Rule 1 with both prongs rising away: the 102cm muon has a monotone 150k Bragg decaying over 8cm at 10000 and the 27cm proton starts near 15k at 10002 and runs 80-120k to its stop, opening at 100 degrees.

Only deg-4 junction in a corner tangle, sitting in a dense 200-480k charge deposit with four prongs leaving in distinct directions; the apparent rule-1 violation is that single shared blob, the hot-blob trap, not four independent Bragg peaks.
Rule 8 event: eleven clusters, every one sub-centimetre, no readable direction anywhere; picked the densest dark-red blob nearest the centroid of the dot cloud, which is close to a pure guess.
The 225cm muon is flat MIP and simply terminates in mid-detector at 18002 with no Bragg, so it is created there, and an 8.5cm proton stub rises 30k to over 120k away at 84 degrees to it.

Clean deg-3 star: the 11.1cm proton rises monotonically along the proton template to 230k at 9005, a 4.7cm hot proton stub leaves to 9004, and the 21.9cm muon runs flat MIP away, with vertex activity at 9003 itself.

Both prongs rise away at 119 degrees: the 19.6cm proton climbs monotonically to a 210k Bragg at 16001 while the 130cm muon runs flat MIP out through the y=-198 bottom face and terminates here with no Bragg.

Rule 1 with two of two rising away at 126 degrees: the 73cm muon ends in a 240k stopping blob at 15000 and the 18cm proton climbs along the proton template to 230k at 15001, so both far ends genuinely stop.

Split between this deg-2 lowest-z junction whose 14cm track rises away and 48036, the apex of the 40cm e-like tangle; 48036 is hot at its head and cools away, so it reads as a stopping end, but the tangle axis back-projects 25cm and 50 degrees off 49045.
